name: Applied Digital Corporation
role: AI data-center developer and lessor; consolidated cloud subsidiary
overview: A Nevada corporation listed on Nasdaq as APLD. The operating story is conversion of contracted campuses into rent: tenant fit-out and controlled ChronoScale also contribute to reported revenue. New lease commitments and project financing remain distinct from delivered critical IT capacity, drawn debt and parent-accessible cash.

size.label: Mid
size.basis: Provider-reported rounded USD equity cap. Mid uses the $2B–<$10B band. The page identifies a November 23 close separately from November 24 premarket trading; cap precision is date-only. Independent shares-through-November-23 reconciliation remains incomplete; no enterprise value or debt/market-cap ratio inferred.

sources.title: Fiscal first quarter 2027 results
sources.excerpt: Revenue from our HPC Hosting business totaled $262.6 million for the quarter, including $65.8 million related to base rent, $183.5 million related to tenant fit-out services, and $13.3 million related to tenant recoveries. ... Those leases represent approximately $36 billion of contracted revenue over their initial base terms ... These non-GAAP measures exclude the results of ChronoScale. ChronoScale ... in which Applied Digital owns approximately 96%.

sources.title: Fiscal fourth quarter and full year 2026 results
sources.excerpt: Revenues: $258.7 million ... ChronoScale, a public company, owns and operates our historic cloud services business and is consolidated into our financial statements, but excluded from the non-GAAP financial measures set forth below. Signed a 15-year take-or-pay lease ... for 300 megawatts ("MW") of critical IT load at Delta Forge 1 ... with initial operations expected to commence calendar year 2027.

sources.title: Polaris Forge 1 Building 2 first phase Ready for Service
sources.excerpt: delivering 75 MW of operational AI capacity to its customer on schedule and bringing total live capacity at the campus to 175 MW. ... At full build out, Polaris Forge 1 is contracted to deliver 400 MW of critical IT load under long-term lease agreements.

sources.title: Additional 75 MW online at Polaris Forge 1
sources.excerpt: The milestone completes Building 2’s full 150 MW of critical IT load and brings fully operational critical IT load at Polaris Forge 1 to 250 MW. The fully leased AI Factory Campus is contracted to deliver 400 MW of critical IT load at full buildout.

sources.title: Delta Forge 1 senior secured bridge facility
sources.excerpt: The bridge facility consists of a $300 million delayed draw term loan with a 364-day maturity, bearing interest at the Secured Overnight Financing Rate (“SOFR”) plus 300 basis points. ... The loan is prepayable at any time without premium and is secured by the assets of the project.

sources.title: New 150 MW, 18-year hyperscaler lease
sources.excerpt: a new 18-year lease agreement with a tier-one investment-grade hyperscaler for 150 MW of critical IT capacity. ... The lease provides for approximately $5.4 billion in base-term contracted revenue ... Delivery of the capacity is currently anticipated to begin in the first half of calendar 2028, subject to applicable development milestones, utility arrangements and regulatory approvals.

changes.before: 175 MW live critical IT at Polaris Forge 1 after the July 1 first phase.
changes.after: 250 MW live critical IT after the second 75 MW phase, reported October 2.
changes.why: Two named primary releases establish an actual capacity increase. A schedule revision cannot be inferred from the delivery dates alone.

changes.before: Approximately $36B of contracted base-term lease revenue reported October 7; renewals separate.
changes.after: Base-term contracted lease revenue exceeds $41B following the new $5.4B, 18-year lease.
changes.why: The signed contract expands the reported lease book. These multi-year amounts are neither recognized quarterly revenue nor unrestricted funding.

changes.before: July 27: Delta Forge 1 had a signed 300 MW, 15-year hyperscaler lease and planned 2027 initial operations. This establishes development context, not a zero-debt starting balance.
changes.after: Closed a $300M delayed-draw project bridge: SOFR + 3.00%, 364-day term. Draws remain conditional; amount funded is undisclosed. Further completion financing is expected.
changes.why: New project financing supports execution of the previously disclosed campus. Closing a commitment does not establish full construction funding or unrestricted cash.

changes.before: October 7: Applied Digital reported approximately 96% ownership of ChronoScale and consolidated its results, while excluding them from adjusted measures. This is dated ownership context.
changes.after: November 20 filing reports the full $97M note funded in the November 18 transaction: APLD lends to ChronoScale, with share conversion conditional on approval effectiveness.
changes.why: A parent-to-subsidiary investment direction, not a new APLD parent debt instrument. Keep the funded note separate from ChronoScale’s conditional Odessa development plan and broader financing framework.

questions: How much of the Delta Forge 1 delayed-draw bridge has actually been funded, and which construction, utility-rate, approval and lender-consent conditions remain?
What financing terms and equity contributions will close the remaining Delta Forge 1 / Polaris Forge 3 funding in Q1 2027 and Delta Forge 2 funding in Q2?
Which campus hosts the new 150 MW lease, and what evidence will establish utility readiness, delivery commencement and tenant acceptance?
Can Polaris Forge 2 reach initial service and the stated North Dakota 300 MW delivered target by the end of 2026? No revised date or outcome has been verified.
How do base rent and cash collections develop relative to fit-out services, which currently account for a large part of HPC revenue?
How much consolidated cash can the parent deploy after project restrictions, reserves and subsidiary obligations? The cash balance is not a parent-only wallet.
How should the changing building names in historical documents be mapped to legal project entities before assigning financing or timeline revisions? No exact numbering bridge is assumed here.
When will the next fiscal-quarter earnings date be confirmed? The issuer calendar still lists no future event at this review.
